notes.definition: Meiosis is the type of cell division in the reproductive organs that makes gametes. It halves the number of chromosomes and produces four genetically different cells, so that fertilisation can restore the full number of chromosomes.
explanation: Body cells contain chromosomes in pairs: human body cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs. If gametes also had 46 chromosomes, the fertilised egg would have 92, and the number would double every generation. Meiosis prevents this. It happens only in the reproductive organs (the testes and ovaries in humans, the anthers and ovaries in flowering plants) and makes gametes that contain a single set of chromosomes, one chromosome from each pair. Human gametes therefore have 23 chromosomes.

When a cell divides by meiosis to form gametes, copies of the genetic information are made first (each chromosome is copied). The cell then divides twice. In the first division the chromosome pairs are separated, so each new cell gets one chromosome from each pair. In the second division the copies of each chromosome are pulled apart. The result is four gametes, each with a single set of chromosomes.

The gametes produced are all genetically different from each other and from the parent cell. This is because the chromosomes from each pair are shared out in different combinations, so each gamete gets a different mixture of the chromosomes originally inherited from the mother and the father. This is one of the main sources of genetic variation in sexual reproduction.

At fertilisation a male gamete and a female gamete join. Each brings one set of chromosomes, so the fertilised egg cell has the full number again, in pairs (23 + 23 = 46 in humans). The new cell then divides repeatedly by mitosis, so the number of cells increases and an embryo forms. As the embryo develops, its cells differentiate into the many specialised cells of the body.

It is important to be able to compare meiosis and mitosis. Mitosis involves one division, produces two cells with the full number of chromosomes and the cells are genetically identical; it is used for growth, repair and asexual reproduction. Meiosis involves two divisions, produces four cells with half the number of chromosomes and the cells are genetically different; it is used only to make gametes.
keyFacts: Meiosis happens in the reproductive organs (testes and ovaries in humans).
The genetic information is copied before the cell divides.
The cell divides twice, forming four gametes.
Each gamete has a single set of chromosomes (one from each pair): 23 in humans.
All the gametes are genetically different from each other.
Fertilisation restores the full number of chromosomes (46 in humans).
After fertilisation the new cell divides by mitosis, and later the embryo's cells differentiate.
Mitosis makes identical cells; meiosis makes non-identical cells.

keyTerms.definition: Cell division in the reproductive organs that produces four genetically different gametes, each with half the normal number of chromosomes.
A sex cell with a single set of chromosomes (one from each pair).
The fusion of a male and a female gamete, which restores the full number of chromosomes.
Two chromosomes carrying the same genes, one inherited from each parent.
The ball of cells that develops from a fertilised egg by repeated mitosis.
The process by which cells become specialised for a particular function.
Cell division that produces two genetically identical cells with the full number of chromosomes.

workedExamples.title: Chromosome numbers through meiosis and fertilisation
workedExamples.question: A chimpanzee body cell has 48 chromosomes. State the number of chromosomes in (a) a chimpanzee sperm cell and (b) a chimpanzee fertilised egg cell.
steps: Meiosis halves the chromosome number: 48 ÷ 2 = 24 in each gamete.
At fertilisation a sperm (24) and an egg (24) fuse: 24 + 24 = 48.
The fertilised egg has the full number again, in 24 pairs.

workedExamples.title: How many gametes?
workedExamples.question: In the testes, 250 cells each divide by meiosis. How many sperm cells are produced?
steps: Meiosis involves two divisions, so each cell produces 4 gametes.

workedExamples.title: Mitosis or meiosis?
workedExamples.question: A cell with 20 chromosomes divides to produce four cells, each with 10 chromosomes. Which type of division is this and where does it happen?
steps: The chromosome number has halved (20 → 10). Only meiosis does this.
Four cells were produced from one, which also matches meiosis (two divisions).
Meiosis makes gametes, so it takes place in the reproductive organs.
workedExamples.answer: Meiosis, in the reproductive organs (for example the testes, ovaries or anthers).

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think meiosis makes two cells.
misconceptions.right: In fact the cell divides twice, so meiosis makes four cells (gametes). Mitosis is the division that makes two cells.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think gametes contain 23 pairs of chromosomes.
misconceptions.right: In fact human gametes contain 23 single chromosomes, one from each pair. The pairs are only restored at fertilisation.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the fertilised egg grows into an embryo by meiosis.
misconceptions.right: In fact after fertilisation all the cell division is by mitosis. Meiosis only happens when gametes are made.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the gametes made by one person are all genetically identical.
misconceptions.right: In fact every gamete is genetically different because the chromosomes from each pair are shared out in different combinations.

realWorld: Errors in meiosis can produce a gamete with an extra chromosome. If an egg with an extra chromosome 21 is fertilised, the child has Down's syndrome.
Fertility clinics study sperm and egg cells, and understanding meiosis helps explain why some embryos do not develop normally.
Plant breeders rely on meiosis producing genetically different pollen and egg cells to create new combinations of features in crops.
examTips: Use the number 'four' for the cells produced by meiosis and 'two' for mitosis; examiners often test this.
Say gametes have 'a single set of chromosomes' or 'one chromosome from each pair', not 'half the genes'.
In 'explain how chromosome number is kept constant' questions, give both halves: meiosis halves the number, fertilisation restores it.
Remember the order of events: copy genetic information, divide twice, four genetically different gametes.
summary: Meiosis happens in reproductive organs to make gametes.
Genetic information is copied, then the cell divides twice.
Four gametes are made, each with a single set of chromosomes.
Fertilisation restores the full chromosome number.
The fertilised egg divides by mitosis; embryo cells then differentiate.
Meiosis gives non-identical cells; mitosis gives identical cells.

flashcards.back: 23 (a single set, one from each pair).

flashcards.back: No, they are all genetically different.

questions.question: Name the type of cells that meiosis produces.
markScheme: 1 mark: gametes
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces gametes (sex cells). Body cells are made by mitosis.

questions.question:
One cell divides by meiosis.
How many cells are produced?
markScheme: 1 mark: 4
questions.explanation: The cell divides twice in meiosis, so one cell gives four gametes. Mitosis gives two cells.

questions.question:
Human body cells contain 46 chromosomes.
How many chromosomes are in a human egg cell?
markScheme: 1 mark: 23
questions.explanation: A human egg cell has 23 single chromosomes, one from each pair. 46 is the body cell number, and the chromosomes are not in pairs in a gamete.

questions.question: Where does meiosis happen in the human body?
markScheme: 1 mark: testes and ovaries
questions.explanation: Meiosis happens only in the reproductive organs because its job is to make gametes. Skin, bone marrow and liver cells divide by mitosis.

questions.question: Which statement describes the gametes produced by meiosis?
options: Genetically identical, with the full number of chromosomes
Genetically identical, with half the number of chromosomes
Genetically different, with half the number of chromosomes
Genetically different, with the full number of chromosomes
markScheme: 1 mark: genetically different, with half the number of chromosomes
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and shares out the chromosomes in different combinations, so the gametes are all genetically different.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the human life cycle.
Which process happens at Y?
markScheme: 1 mark: it divides by mitosis
questions.explanation: Process Y turns the fertilised egg into an embryo. The fertilised egg divides repeatedly by mitosis, so all embryo cells have the same genetic information. Meiosis only makes gametes, and cells must divide before they can differentiate into an embryo.

Copy genetic information, divide once, two gametes form
Divide twice, copy genetic information, four gametes form
Divide once, copy genetic information, two gametes form

Mitosis: 2 cells with 4. Meiosis: 4 cells with 8
Mitosis: 2 cells with 8. Meiosis: 4 cells with 4

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows a cell with two pairs of chromosomes. In each pair, one chromosome came from the mother and one from the father.
The cell divides by meiosis to produce four gametes.
Why are the four gametes genetically different?
options: Each gamete receives a different combination of chromosomes from each pair
The genetic information is not copied before division

questions.explanation: When the pairs separate, each gamete gets one chromosome from each pair, but which one (originally from the mother or father) varies, so the combinations differ. The genetic information is copied before meiosis, and fertilisation happens later.

markScheme: 1 mark: two gametes join / fuse at fertilisation
1 mark: so the fertilised egg has the normal (full) number of chromosomes / number does not double each generation
questions.explanation: Each gamete brings one set; together they give the full set. If gametes had the full number, the chromosome number would double every generation.

questions.question: Describe what happens when a cell in the reproductive organs divides to form gametes.
markScheme: 1 mark: copies of the genetic information (chromosomes) are made
1 mark: the cell divides twice to form four gametes
1 mark: each gamete has a single set of chromosomes / gametes are genetically different
questions.explanation: This is the spec sequence for meiosis: copy, divide twice, four genetically different gametes, each with one set of chromosomes.

questions.question: Give two differences between the cells produced by mitosis and the cells produced by meiosis.
acceptedAnswers: full chromosome number compared with half
markScheme: 1 mark each, any two (must compare): mitosis makes 2 cells, meiosis makes 4; mitosis cells genetically identical, meiosis cells genetically different; mitosis cells have the full number of chromosomes, meiosis cells have half; mitosis makes body cells, meiosis makes gametes
questions.explanation: Differences must refer to both processes. Compare number of cells, chromosome number and whether they are genetically identical.

questions.question: Describe what happens to a fertilised egg cell after fertilisation.
markScheme: 1 mark: divides by mitosis / number of cells increases (to form an embryo)
1 mark: cells differentiate (become specialised) as the embryo develops
questions.explanation: The new cell divides by mitosis to make an embryo, and as it develops its cells differentiate into specialised cells.

questions.question: Explain how meiosis and fertilisation keep the chromosome number of a species constant from one generation to the next, and also produce variation.
markScheme: 1 mark: meiosis halves the chromosome number / gametes have one set
1 mark: fertilisation joins two gametes, restoring the full (paired) number
1 mark: gametes are genetically different and fusion of gametes from two parents (random) gives new combinations, so offspring vary
questions.explanation: Halving then restoring keeps the number constant. Variation arises because each gamete has a unique combination of chromosomes and fertilisation randomly brings together gametes from two parents.

questions.question:
A mule is the offspring of a male donkey and a female horse.
Table 1 shows the number of chromosomes in the body cells of a horse and a donkey.
Calculate the number of chromosomes in a mule body cell.
Suggest why a mule cannot carry out normal meiosis.
markScheme: 1 mark: chromosomes are not in matching pairs (odd number), so they cannot separate properly into gametes
questions.explanation: The horse gamete has 32 and the donkey gamete has 31, giving 63. Meiosis relies on chromosomes being in pairs that separate, so an odd, unmatched set means normal gametes cannot form and mules are usually infertile.

headers: Number of chromosomes in a body cell

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the chromosomes from one body cell of a pea plant, arranged in pairs.
How many chromosomes are in a pea pollen gamete?
markScheme: 1 mark: 7
questions.explanation: Figure 1 shows 7 pairs, so a body cell has 14 chromosomes. Meiosis halves the chromosome number: 14 ÷ 2 = 7.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the number of chromosomes in the gametes of some animals.
Calculate the number of chromosomes in a horse body cell.
markScheme: 1 mark: 64
questions.explanation: Gametes have half the body cell number, so body cells have 32 × 2 = 64 chromosomes.

headers: Number of chromosomes in a gamete

questions.question:
In an ovary, 1200 cells divide by meiosis.
Calculate the total number of cells produced when all 1200 cells have finished dividing.
markScheme: 1 mark: each cell produces 4 cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis involves two divisions, so each cell gives four. 1200 × 4 = 4800. (In humans most of the cells formed in the ovary do not become eggs, but the number of cells produced by the divisions is still four per cell.)

questions.question:
A fertilised egg divides by mitosis. Every cell then divides again every 12 hours.
Calculate the number of cells in the embryo after 3 days.
Assume all the cells keep dividing.
markScheme: 1 mark: number of divisions = 72 ÷ 12 = 6
1 mark: 2⁶ = 64
questions.explanation: 3 days = 72 hours, so 6 divisions. The number doubles each time: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the number of chromosomes in a body cell of three animals.
How many pairs of chromosomes does a chicken fertilised egg cell contain?
markScheme: 1 mark: 39
questions.explanation: A fertilised egg has the full number, 78, which is arranged as 78 ÷ 2 = 39 pairs (one chromosome of each pair from each parent).

headers: Number of chromosomes in a body cell

questions.question: What is restored when a sperm cell fertilises an egg cell?
markScheme: 1 mark: the full number of chromosomes
questions.explanation: Each gamete has a single set of chromosomes, so fusion restores the full paired number.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows a cell with 6 chromosomes dividing to form two cells.
A student labels Figure 1 as meiosis.
Why is the student wrong?
options: Meiosis produces four cells each with 3 chromosomes
Meiosis produces two cells with 3 chromosomes
markScheme: 1 mark: meiosis produces four cells each with 3 chromosomes
questions.explanation: Figure 1 shows mitosis: two genetically identical cells, each with the full number of 6 chromosomes. Meiosis would give four cells, each with half the number (3).

questions.question: Name one organ in a flowering plant where meiosis takes place.
markScheme: 1 mark: anther or ovary (accept ovule, stamen)
questions.explanation: Plant gametes are made in the anthers (pollen) and the ovaries (egg cells), so meiosis happens there.

questions.question: Compare mitosis and meiosis.
markScheme: Indicative content: mitosis one division, meiosis two divisions; mitosis two cells, meiosis four; mitosis cells have full chromosome number, meiosis cells have half (single set); mitosis cells genetically identical, meiosis cells genetically different; mitosis for growth, repair and asexual reproduction, meiosis makes gametes; mitosis throughout the body, meiosis only in reproductive organs; both involve copying genetic information first.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): at least three clear comparisons, with both processes referred to in each.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, mostly about one process.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Good answers use comparative language ('whereas', 'but') and cover number of cells, chromosome number, genetic identity and where or why each happens.

questions.question: Human body cells contain 46 chromosomes. Explain how a new human, whose body cells contain 46 chromosomes and who is genetically different from both parents, is produced from the cells of two parents. Refer to cell division and fertilisation in your answer.
markScheme: Indicative content: meiosis in testes and ovaries; genetic information copied; cell divides twice; four gametes; each with 23 chromosomes (single set, one of each pair); gametes genetically different (different combinations of chromosomes); fertilisation: sperm (23) and egg (23) fuse to give 46 (23 pairs), one of each pair from each parent; random which gametes fuse; mixing of genetic information from two parents gives variation; fertilised egg divides by mitosis; number of cells increases to form embryo; mitosis copies genetic information exactly so all body cells have 46; cells differentiate as embryo develops.

Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): a detailed, logically linked explanation covering meiosis halving the number with genetically different gametes, fertilisation restoring 46 with mixing of genetic information, and growth by mitosis with differentiation.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explains meiosis halving the number and fertilisation restoring it, with some reference to variation or mitosis.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, for example that sperm and egg each have 23 chromosomes and join.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: The answer must link the process to both outcomes: the constant number (halving by meiosis, restoring at fertilisation, kept by mitosis) and variation (different gametes, random fusion, genes from two parents).

questions.question: Which process increases the number of cells in a developing embryo?
markScheme: 1 mark: mitosis
questions.explanation: After fertilisation the cell divides repeatedly by mitosis. Differentiation changes the type of cell but does not increase the number.

questions.question: Give the number of times a cell divides during meiosis.
markScheme: 1 mark: twice
questions.explanation: Meiosis involves two divisions, which is why four gametes are formed.
